Docker Commands

Building & Running Containers

  • Build an image: sh docker build -t node-image-app . -t is used to specify the image name.
  • Run a container: sh docker run -it --rm -p 4000:4000 -d --name <container-name> <image-id>
    • -p 4000:4000 → Maps port 4000 of the container to port 4000 on the host.
    • -d → Runs the container in detached mode.
    • --name → Assigns a custom name to the container. -it ---> opens the terminal --rm --> removes when we exit the container

Managing Containers & Images

  • List all running containers: sh docker ps
  • List all containers (including stopped ones): sh docker ps -a
  • List all images: sh docker image ls
  • Pull an image from Docker Hub: sh docker pull <image-name>
  • Stop a container: sh docker stop <container-id>
  • Start a container: sh docker start <container-id>
  • Remove a container: sh docker rm <container-id> -f # -f forces removal
  • Remove an image: sh docker rmi <image-id>

Running Commands Inside a Container

  • Access a running container: sh docker exec -it <container-id> bash This allows interactive access to the container’s shell.
  • View logs from a container: sh docker logs <container-name> -f
  • Inspect container details: sh docker inspect <container-id>

Docker Volumes & Mounts

Bind Mounts

  • Run a container with a bind mount: sh docker run -v <local-dir>:<container-dir>:<permissions> -p 4000:4000 -d <image-id>
    • permissions: ro for read-only access. docker run -it --rm --mount type=bind,source="${PWD}"/my-data,destination=/my-data ubuntu:22.04

Docker Volumes

  • List all volumes: sh docker volume ls
  • Remove unused volumes: sh docker volume prune
  • Remove a volume when deleting a container: sh docker rm <container-id> -fv
  • Remove a specific volume: sh docker volume rm <volume-name>

Create a container and mount the volume into the container filesystem

docker run -it --rm --mount source=my-volume,destination=/my-data/ ubuntu:22.04

Docker Compose

Basic Commands

  • Start containers: sh docker-compose up
  • Stop and remove containers, networks, and volumes: sh docker-compose down -v
  • Start in detached mode and force a rebuild: sh docker-compose up -d --build
  • Use multiple compose files: sh docker-compose -f <file1.yml> -f <file2.yml> up -d --build
  • Scale a service: sh docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --scale <service-name>=2
